summary: The 4 new yuzu_fleet_perf_os_* Prometheus gauge families clear themselves INSIDE the new recompute_perf_os_gauges helper (called near the bottom of recompute_metrics, line ~2428) instead of in that function's established top-of-function clear-everything-before-rebuild block where every sibling family (including the analogous yuzu_fleet_net_*{os}) is cleared. As shipped this is inert -- cpp-expert, sre and chaos-injector each independently confirmed via full-function grep that no early return exists in recompute_metrics between the top clear block and line 2428, so every sweep correctly clears-then-rebuilds all 4 new families today (E6: the wrong outcome is proven unable to occur in current production code). The risk is structural: a plausible future fast-path optimization (e.g. an early return when snapshots_ is empty) would silently exempt only these 4 families from the absent-not-zero guarantee every other family in this function keeps, freezing stale non-zero per-OS values indefinitely on every subsequent scrape -- and no existing test would catch it (test_agent_health_store.cpp's new C1 per-OS test only exercises a single recompute_metrics call, never the populate-then-resweep-without-data sequence the pre-existing sibling absent-not-zero tests use). Cheap, mechanical fix: hoist the 4 clear_gauge_family calls into the existing top-of-function block.
classification_rationale: not a doc/wording issue -- the function's own doc comment on recompute_perf_os_gauges implies it follows the same absent-not-zero discipline as its siblings, but its clear+rebuild coupling structurally differs from every other family in the same function

Recommendation (non-blocking): a one-line cross-reference in docs/user-manual/metrics.md's new per-OS section (documented as a should-fix, not required for this slice), and tightening it into an explicit C5 (macOS-collector slice) prerequisite so a future SRE building a Grafana panel against the only-documented-with-a-worked-example os="macos" convention does not get silent empty results the day real macOS perf data starts flowing under os="darwin" instead.
classification_rationale: docs/user-manual/metrics.md (this diff) correctly and separately documents the darwin token for this surface and dex.md/rest-api.md correctly document macos for theirs -- each surface's own doc is accurate, but nothing cross-references the two conventions as describing the same underlying fact

trigger: an enrolled agent reporting a non-canonical-case AgentSession.os / yuzu.os heartbeat tag value (e.g. "Windows"/"WINDOWS"/"Darwin" with a capital letter) -- normalize_os (agent_registry.cpp, Prometheus path) is a case-SENSITIVE exact match and folds any non-lowercase-canonical value into its generic "other" bucket, while dex_perf_os_from_session (dex_perf_rules.hpp, REST/MCP/dashboard path) lowercases before its prefix match and classifies the identical string correctly; every shipped Yuzu agent build emits the exact lowercase canonical kAgentOs token today, so this requires a non-conformant, third-party, or adversarial-but-already-enrolled agent build, not standard fleet operation
summary: A NEW, worse-in-kind (full bucket misclassification rather than a label-spelling mismatch) instance of the darwin/macos-class domain gap between the two closed-set OS normalizers, found during chaos-injector's Gate 5 pass. Unlike the darwin/macos split (F3), this one is reachable TODAY without waiting for a macOS collector: any non-canonical-case OS string an agent reports is silently folded into Prometheus's os="other" catch-all (agent_registry.cpp's pre-existing normalize_os lambda, untouched by C1 but newly exercised by the perf-os families this diff adds), while the REST/MCP/dashboard path (dex_perf_os_from_session, this diff) correctly classifies the same string via its own lowercasing prefix match. Net effect: a per-OS Prometheus bucket can silently undercount by one device while the REST/MCP aggregate for the same OS remains correct -- an observability-only discrepancy, not a data-loss or security issue; the underlying per-device data and every other surface remain fully correct, only the Prometheus os-family BUCKET for that one non-conformant device is imprecise. Bounded to fleets running a non-standard agent build (the field is documented in the code's own comment as agent-controlled/untrusted, same trust boundary as enrollment generally). Strengthens, does not duplicate, the F3 remediation: unifying the two normalizers into one shared, case-insensitive, closed-set function closes both gaps in the same change.
classification_rationale: not a doc/wording issue -- a behavioral domain-boundary gap between two independently-implemented classification functions over the same untrusted input
